note: Compiled and paraphrased from publicly shared candidate experiences. Not official; actual tests may differ.

bank.q: In a classical cryogenic double-column Air Separation Unit (ASU), what thermodynamic link connects the high-pressure column (operating at ~5-6 bar) and the low-pressure column (operating at ~1.3-1.5 bar)?
options: A shared main condenser-reboiler where condensing high-pressure nitrogen vapor at the top of the HP column vaporizes boiling liquid oxygen at the bottom of the LP column
A high-pressure centrifugal steam injector
An electric resistance heater installed between the columns
A liquid nitrogen expansion engine discharging into the atmosphere
bank.explain: At 5.5 bar, nitrogen condenses at ~96 K, which is slightly warmer than the boiling temperature of pure liquid oxygen at 1.4 bar (~93 K). This temperature difference enables heat transfer in the main condenser-reboiler without external heat input.

bank.q: What thermodynamic parameter determines whether a real gas cools or heats upon undergoing an isenthalpic expansion across a throttling valve (Joule-Thomson effect)?
options: The critical compressibility factor Z_c
The Joule-Thomson coefficient: mu_JT = (d T / d P)_H; cooling occurs when mu_JT > 0, which requires the gas temperature to be below its maximum inversion temperature
The standard enthalpy of formation
The kinematic viscosity ratio
bank.explain: In an isenthalpic throttle, dT = mu_JT * dP. Since dP < 0, dT < 0 (cooling) only if mu_JT > 0. For gases like air, N2, and O2, ambient temperature is well below their maximum inversion temperature (~600 K), producing cooling upon depressurization.

bank.q: In modern cryogenic ASUs, why is ambient air passed through a Temperature Swing Adsorption (TSA) molecular sieve bed prior to cryogenic cooling?
options: To separate nitrogen from oxygen before entering the cold box
To convert atmospheric oxygen into ozone

To remove moisture (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and heavy hydrocarbons down to ppb/ppm levels to prevent freeze-plugging in cryogenic exchangers and catastrophic explosion risks in the liquid oxygen bath
To add neon and helium tracer gases
bank.explain: Water and CO2 freeze as solids at cryogenic temperatures, plugging brazed aluminum heat exchangers. Furthermore, atmospheric hydrocarbons (acetylene, ethane) concentrate in the liquid oxygen sump, presenting a severe detonation hazard if not captured.

bank.q: Why are Brazed Aluminum Heat Exchangers (BAHX), commonly known as plate-fin heat exchangers, universally specified in ASU cold boxes?
options: They eliminate the need for thermal insulation around the cold box
They can withstand temperatures above 1200 C
They are immune to galvanic corrosion in concentrated nitric acid

They provide exceptionally high surface area density (up to 1500 m^2/m^3), allow multiple process streams to exchange heat simultaneously within a single compact block, and offer high thermal conductivity and ductility at cryogenic temperatures
bank.explain: Cryogenic ASUs require minute temperature approaches (1 to 2 K) between warming and cooling streams to minimize thermodynamic irreversibility. BAHX blocks provide immense heat transfer area in a compact footprint with multi-stream integration.

bank.q: Why is the accumulation of trace acetylene (C2H2) and other hydrocarbons in the liquid oxygen (LOX) sump of an ASU main condenser strictly monitored and limited to < 0.1 ppm?
options: Acetylene has very low solubility in liquid oxygen; precipitated solid acetylene crystals can detonate upon slight mechanical friction or electrostatic discharge in pure oxygen
Acetylene reacts with aluminum to dissolve the heat exchanger fins
Acetylene vaporizes and increases column operating pressure uncontrollably
Acetylene freezes into insulating foam that stops heat transfer
bank.explain: Solid acetylene is notoriously unstable and sensitive. In pure LOX, solid crystals act as a primary explosive initiator, triggering violent combustion of aluminum in liquid oxygen. Continuous liquid oxygen purge and online GC monitoring are mandatory.

bank.q: In cryogenic refrigeration cycles, what is the thermodynamic advantage of expanding high-pressure gas through a turboexpander (work-producing isentropic expansion) compared to an isenthalpic throttle valve?
options: Isentropic expansion heats the gas, increasing column reboiler duty

Isentropic expansion extracts shaft work (Delta H = W_shaft), producing substantially greater temperature drop and generating refrigeration without relying solely on non-ideal gas intermolecular forces
Turboexpanders eliminate the need for compressor suction filters
Turboexpanders double the pressure of the expanding fluid
bank.explain: An isenthalpic valve conserves enthalpy (Delta H = 0), yielding modest Joule-Thomson cooling. An isentropic turboexpander extracts energy as mechanical shaft power, causing a steep enthalpy reduction and much deeper cooling.

bank.q: Why is argon separation from air considered one of the most challenging cryogenic distillation operations?
options: Argon reacts chemically with stainless steel packing to form argon fluoride
Argon forms a solid clathrate with liquid nitrogen at ambient pressure

The boiling points of oxygen (-183.0 C) and argon (-185.9 C) are extremely close (relative volatility alpha ~ 1.1), and argon reaches a peak concentration of only ~10-15 mol% midway up the low-pressure column
Argon cannot be condensed into a liquid under any pressure
bank.explain: Argon's boiling point lies between nitrogen (-195.8 C) and oxygen (-183.0 C), with very low relative volatility against oxygen. Pure argon recovery requires a dedicated side-arm column with over 150-200 structured packing stages.

bank.q: In high-pressure industrial gas cylinders (such as 200 bar gaseous nitrogen), why must manifold valves be opened slowly when connecting to dead-end piping?
options: Rapid opening ionizes the nitrogen into corrosive plasma
Slow opening prevents nitrogen from turning into liquid inside the pipe
Fast opening creates a vacuum that collapses the steel cylinder walls
Rapid gas compression in the dead-end pipe causes near-adiabatic compressive heating, which can generate localized temperatures exceeding the auto-ignition limit of valve seats and seal materials
bank.explain: Adiabatic compression of gas in a dead-end tube can heat stagnant gas to > 500 C in microseconds. In oxygen systems, this easily ignites polymeric valve packings, causing disastrous valve fires.

bank.q: Why is structured corrugated sheet packing (such as Mellapak) favored over sieve trays in ASU low-pressure columns and crude argon columns?
options: Structured packing exhibits an extremely low pressure drop per theoretical stage (0.2-0.5 mbar/stage), minimizing reboiler bottom pressure and reducing main air compressor power consumption
Packing is cheaper than simple drilled carbon steel sheets
Structured packing eliminates the need for liquid distributors
Packing allows the column to operate upside down
bank.explain: In an ASU, pressure drop across the LP column directly raises the bottom pressure, which raises the boiling temperature of oxygen and forces the HP column to operate at higher pressure, increasing compressor power.

bank.q: In cryogenic vacuum-insulated pipe (VIP) and storage tanks, what is the purpose of combining multi-layer insulation (MLI / superinsulation) with high vacuum (< 10^-4 mbar)?
options: Vacuum prevents atmospheric oxygen from rusting the inner container
The high vacuum eliminates gas conduction and natural convection, while alternating reflective aluminum foil and low-conductivity spacer layers minimize radiant heat transfer
MLI reflects sound waves generated by boiling cryogenic liquid
The vacuum increases the mechanical tensile strength of the outer carbon steel jacket
bank.explain: At pressures below 10^-4 mbar, the mean free path of gas molecules exceeds the gap distance, eliminating convective/conductive heat transfer. Multi-layer radiation shields reduce radiation by a factor of 1/(N+1).

bank.q: Hydrogen gas has a Joule-Thomson inversion temperature of approximately 202 K (-71 C) at atmospheric pressure. What does this imply for hydrogen liquefaction?
options: Hydrogen will freeze into solid crystals if expanded through a valve at room temperature
Hydrogen can be liquefied by simple throttling directly from ambient room temperature
Hydrogen throttled at ambient temperature (300 K) will heat up rather than cool down; it must be pre-cooled below 202 K (typically using liquid nitrogen at 77 K) before throttling can produce cooling
Hydrogen cannot be compressed to pressures exceeding 2 bar
bank.explain: Because mu_JT is negative above the inversion temperature, throttling un-precooled hydrogen causes heating, risking autoignition. Hydrogen must be chilled with liquid nitrogen before JT cooling or expanded through work-extracting turbines.

bank.q: Why must hydrogen liquefiers incorporate catalytic ortho-to-para conversion catalysts (such as ferric oxide or ruthenium on alumina) during cooling?
options: The conversion increases the density of liquid hydrogen by a factor of ten
Para-hydrogen is explosive, while ortho-hydrogen is completely inert
Ortho-hydrogen solidifies at 50 K, plugging transfer lines

At room temperature, normal hydrogen is 75% ortho and 25% para; the slow uncatalyzed conversion of ortho to para in liquid storage releases 703 kJ/kg of heat (exceeding liquid hydrogen's latent heat of 446 kJ/kg), which would boil off the entire liquid inventory
bank.explain: The nuclear spin state equilibrium shifts to 99.8% para-hydrogen at 20 K. If not catalytically converted during liquefaction, the slow exothermic spin transition in storage boils off all stored liquid.

bank.q: A liquid nitrogen pump pressurizes cryogenic LN2 from 1.2 bar to 30 bar. Assuming liquid nitrogen is incompressible with density 800 kg/m^3, what is the ideal pump hydraulic work per kilogram (W = Delta P / rho)?
What is the primary asphyxiation danger associated with gaseous nitrogen (N2) leaks in enclosed industrial spaces?
options: Nitrogen produces intense bronchial burning and coughing that paralyzes the vocal cords

Nitrogen is completely odorless, colorless, and tasteless; breathing an oxygen-deficient atmosphere (O2 < 10%) causes sudden unconsciousness within one or two breaths without any prior dyspnea or warning symptoms
Nitrogen reacts with room air to produce toxic nitrogen dioxide smoke
Nitrogen gas causes rapid flash fires when exposed to static sparks
bank.explain: The human body detects carbon dioxide buildup, not oxygen deficiency. In pure nitrogen atmospheres, oxygen rapidly diffuses out of pulmonary blood, causing instantaneous cerebral hypoxia and blackout.

bank.q: Why is multi-stage intercooled centrifugal compression used for the Main Air Compressor (MAC) in large ASU plants instead of a single adiabatic compression stage?
options: Single-stage compression causes air to liquefy immediately inside the impeller
Multi-stage compression generates hot flue gas for steam generation

Intercooling brings the compression path closer to isothermal compression, which drastically minimizes the total electrical compression power required and keeps discharge temperatures safely within mechanical limits
Intercooling eliminates the need for electric motors
bank.explain: Isothermal compression requires minimum work (integral of V dP). Interstage water coolers reduce gas temperature between stages, reducing specific volume and slashing power demand by 15-25%.

bank.q: In a Vacuum Pressure Swing Adsorption (VPSA) unit producing oxygen at 93% purity for steel mills, what adsorbent selectively retains nitrogen over oxygen?
options: Activated bauxite pellets
Granular coconut shell activated carbon
Hydrophobic silica gel beads
Lithium-exchanged low-silica X-type zeolites (LiLSX), whose high electric field gradient strongly coordinates with the quadrupolar moment of nitrogen molecules
bank.explain: Nitrogen possesses a permanent quadrupole moment three times larger than oxygen. Li+ cations in the zeolite framework interact strongly with nitrogen quadrupoles, allowing oxygen to pass through unadsorbed.

bank.q: Why is standard structural carbon steel strictly prohibited for piping and vessels operating at cryogenic temperatures (e.g., liquid nitrogen at -196 C)?
options: Carbon steel undergoes a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature (DBTT) well above cryogenic levels, causing catastrophic shattering under nominal mechanical stress or pressure
Carbon steel dissolves in contact with liquid nitrogen
Carbon steel becomes an electrical superconductor at -196 C
Carbon steel generates pyrophoric dust when cold
bank.explain: Body-centered cubic (BCC) metals like carbon steel lose dislocation mobility below their DBTT (-20 C to -40 C), fracturing brittly. Face-centered cubic (FCC) alloys (austenitic stainless steel 304L, aluminum 5083, copper) have no DBTT.

bank.q: What type of flow meter is preferred for custody-transfer metering of large-volume cryogenic liquid transfers to road tankers?
options: Standard pitot tubes with mercury manometers
Cryogenic Coriolis mass flow meters, which measure true mass flow directly without requiring temperature-density pressure corrections
Rotameters with plastic floats
Orifice plates with uninsulated impulse tubing
bank.explain: Coriolis meters measure true mass flow directly via Coriolis acceleration in vibrating tubes, unaffected by boiling vapor bubbles or fluid density changes, making them the gold standard for cryogenic custody transfer.

bank.q: An air separation plant compresses 60,000 Nm^3/h of air. If atmospheric air contains 21 mol% oxygen and the overall oxygen recovery is 98%, how many Nm^3/h of pure gaseous oxygen are produced?
bank.explain: Total oxygen in feed = 60,000 * 0.21 = 12,600 Nm^3/h. Pure oxygen recovered = 12,600 * 0.98 = 12,348 Nm^3/h.

bank.q: A cryogenic liquid nitrogen storage vessel holds 40,000 liters of LN2. If the normal daily boil-off rate is 0.5% of the initial volume, how many liters of liquid nitrogen boil off over a 10-day period?
options: 1,500 liters
1,800 liters
2,500 liters
2,000 liters
bank.explain: Daily boil-off = 40,000 * 0.005 = 200 liters/day. Over 10 days = 200 * 10 = 2,000 liters.

bank.q: A gas cylinder with an internal volume of 50 liters is filled with argon at 200 bar and 300 K. Assuming ideal gas behavior (PV = nRT with R = 0.08314 bar*L/(mol*K)), approximately how many moles of argon are contained in the cylinder?
options: 401 moles
350 moles
480 moles
250 moles

bank.q: A liquid oxygen pump motor operates at 45 kW. If electricity costs $0.08 per kWh and the pump runs continuously for 30 days (720 hours), what is the total monthly power cost?
bank.explain: Energy consumed = 45 kW * 720 h = 32,400 kWh. Total cost = 32,400 * $0.08 = $2,592.

bank.q: Identify the missing number in the sequence: 3, 12, 48, 192, ?
bank.explain: Each number is multiplied by 4: 3*4=12; 12*4=48; 48*4=192; 192*4=768.

bank.q: Statements: All industrial gas plants require refrigeration. Some refrigeration systems operate at cryogenic temperatures. Which statement is logically valid?
options: No industrial gas plant uses refrigeration
All industrial gas plants operate at cryogenic temperatures
Cryogenic temperatures cannot be achieved by refrigeration
Some systems operating at cryogenic temperatures are refrigeration systems
bank.explain: The sub-statement 'Some refrigeration systems operate at cryogenic temperatures' directly converts to 'Some systems operating at cryogenic temperatures are refrigeration systems'.

bank.q: In a control room code, 'OXYGEN' is written as 'PZZHFO'. Each letter is shifted: O(+1)->P, X(+2)->Z, Y(+1)->Z, G(+1)->H, E(+1)->F, N(+1)->O. If every letter is simply shifted forward by 1 position in a standard cipher, how is 'ARGON' encoded?
options: BSHPO
BSHQO
CRHPO
BRGPN
bank.explain: Shift each letter forward by 1: A+1=B, R+1=S, G+1=H, O+1=P, N+1=O -> BSHPO.

bank.q: An ASU plant generates product revenues: Liquid Oxygen 40%, Gaseous Oxygen 30%, Liquid Nitrogen 20%, Argon 10%. If total monthly revenue is $1,500,000, how much revenue is generated by Argon?
Select the word most similar in meaning (synonym) to 'ISENTROPIC':
options: Isobaric
Isothermal
Reversible adiabatic
Isochoric
bank.explain: An isentropic process is one in which entropy remains constant, which for an ideal system corresponds to an idealized internally reversible adiabatic process.

bank.q: Choose the correct phrase to complete the safety rule: 'Personnel entering the cold box enclosed area must carry a calibrated oxygen monitor _______ prevent unnoticed asphyxiation.'
options: in case of
although
even though
so as to
bank.explain: 'So as to' correctly denotes purpose or intention in formal grammatical construction.

interview.about: Linde is the world's largest industrial gases and engineering enterprise, designing, building, and operating cryogenic air separation units, hydrogen and synthesis gas plants, and gas processing complexes. Linde recruits chemical engineers for cryogenic process design, plant commissioning, onsite operations engineering, and clean hydrogen technology.
looks_for: Deep mastery of thermodynamics, cryogenic phase equilibria, refrigeration cycles, and heat transfer.
Uncompromising approach to process safety, especially oxygen compatibility and cryogenic hazards.
Strong analytical and mathematical capability in sizing compressors, heat exchangers, and distillation columns.
Demonstrated ownership, field readiness, and operational discipline in managing complex gas processing plants.
Curiosity and technical vision for green hydrogen, CCUS, and industrial decarbonization.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills across global engineering execution centers.
selection: Standardized digital assessment evaluating numerical calculation, deductive logic, and engineering aptitude.
Preliminary behavioral and competency interview exploring teamwork, communication, and safety mindset.
Comprehensive technical interview panel with process design authorities and plant operations managers on thermodynamics and plant flows.
Final leadership discussion reviewing organizational culture fit, career aspirations, and geographical mobility.

technical.q: Explain the fundamental working principle of the Linde double-column cryogenic air separation system.
technical.a: Purified air enters the High Pressure (HP) column at ~5.5 bar and separates into high-purity nitrogen vapor overhead and oxygen-enriched rich liquid (approx. 38% O2) at the bottom. Nitrogen vapor condenses in the main condenser-reboiler against boiling liquid oxygen at the bottom of the Low Pressure (LP) column (~1.3 bar). The condensed nitrogen provides reflux for both columns, while rich liquid flashes into the LP column where final separation yields ultra-high purity oxygen at the bottom and waste nitrogen overhead.

technical.q: Why is the main condenser-reboiler able to operate without any external heating or cooling utility?
technical.a: Because boiling temperature increases with pressure. At 5.5 bar, nitrogen condenses at approximately 96 K, which is roughly 3 K warmer than pure liquid oxygen boiling at 1.4 bar (~93 K). This positive temperature difference allows condensing nitrogen vapor to provide the reboiling duty for oxygen across the aluminum plate-fin passages, simultaneously generating liquid nitrogen reflux and boiling gaseous oxygen.

technical.q: What causes severe explosion hazards in the liquid oxygen sump of an ASU, and how are they engineered out?
technical.a: Atmospheric hydrocarbons (such as acetylene, ethylene, and methane) that slip through the front-end purification unit dissolve in liquid oxygen. Acetylene has very low solubility and precipitates as solid crystals, which can detonate upon slight impact or friction in pure LOX. Mitigations include molecular sieve pre-purification, continuous liquid oxygen liquid sump purge (1-2% of production) to prevent concentration buildup, and automated online gas chromatograph monitoring.

technical.q: Explain the thermodynamic difference between isentropic expansion in a turboexpander and isenthalpic expansion across a JT valve.
technical.a: An isenthalpic Joule-Thomson expansion occurs at constant enthalpy (Delta H = 0) with zero external work performed, depending solely on non-ideal intermolecular forces to produce temperature drop (dT = mu_JT * dP). An isentropic expansion in a turbine extracts mechanical shaft work (Delta H = W_shaft), producing a much steeper temperature drop regardless of whether the gas is ideal or non-ideal, delivering vastly more refrigeration per unit mass.

technical.q: Why are Brazed Aluminum Heat Exchangers (BAHX) used in ASU cold boxes instead of conventional shell-and-tube exchangers?
technical.a: Cryogenic separation requires tiny temperature approaches (1 to 2 K) to minimize exergy loss. BAHX provides enormous surface area density (up to 1500 m^2/m^3) and allows up to 10 or more different process streams to exchange heat concurrently within a single brazed core. Aluminum also retains high ductility, impact resistance, and thermal conductivity at temperatures below -200 C.

technical.q: How is argon separated from air given the close boiling points of argon and oxygen?
technical.a: Argon boils at -185.9 C, between nitrogen (-195.8 C) and oxygen (-183.0 C). A vapor sidestream is withdrawn from the low-pressure column at the tray with the peak argon concentration (~10-12% Ar, balance O2) and fed to a crude argon column containing over 150-200 stages of structured packing. Because the relative volatility is only ~1.1, high reflux from an overhead condenser cooled by rich liquid is required to separate crude argon (> 98% Ar).

technical.q: What is the purpose of front-end Temperature Swing Adsorption (TSA) molecular sieve units in ASUs?
technical.a: Ambient air contains water vapor, carbon dioxide, and trace hydrocarbons. At cryogenic temperatures, water and CO2 freeze into solids, plugging heat exchanger passages and column trays. Molecular sieve 13X beds adsorb moisture down to < 0.1 ppm and CO2 down to < 0.5 ppm at ambient temperatures, and are periodically regenerated with warm dry waste nitrogen at ~150-200 C.

technical.q: Why is material selection critical in high-pressure pure oxygen piping systems?
technical.a: In pure high-pressure oxygen, standard carbon steel and many metals can ignite and sustain combustion if particle impingement, high flow velocity, or adiabatic compression creates localized friction or heat. Oxygen systems use velocity-limited design, stringent cleaning for oxygen service (CFOS) to eliminate grease/oils, and non-flammable noble alloys like Monel, Inconel, or copper alloys in throttling valves and impingement zones.

technical.q: How does an internal compression (pumped LOX) ASU process differ from external gaseous oxygen compression?
technical.a: In external compression, low-pressure gaseous oxygen is withdrawn from the column and compressed in an external multi-stage centrifugal compressor. In internal compression, liquid oxygen is pumped directly from the sump to high pressure (up to 40-70 bar) using a cryogenic liquid pump and then vaporized inside high-pressure BAHX passages against high-pressure air. Internal compression eliminates hazardous high-pressure gaseous oxygen compressors, improving safety and reliability.

technical.q: Explain the significance of the ortho-to-para conversion in cryogenic liquid hydrogen storage.
technical.a: Hydrogen exists as two nuclear spin isomers: ortho-hydrogen (parallel nuclear spins) and para-hydrogen (antiparallel spins). Normal hydrogen at ambient temperature is 75% ortho and 25% para. At 20 K, equilibrium favors 99.8% para-hydrogen. The uncatalyzed transition is slow and releases 703 kJ/kg of heat, which is greater than hydrogen's latent heat of vaporization (446 kJ/kg). Without catalytic conversion during liquefaction, the heat of conversion would boil off the liquid in storage.

hr.q: Why do you want to pursue a career with Linde?
hr.how: Highlight Linde's global technology leadership in industrial gases and engineering, its cutting-edge cryogenic and clean hydrogen technology portfolio, and its central role in driving heavy industry decarbonization.

hr.q: Describe a project where you had to perform rigorous mathematical or simulation modeling. How did you ensure accuracy?
hr.how: Explain your validation methodology: verifying thermodynamic property packages, conducting manual order-of-magnitude first-principles hand calculations, performing dimensional checks, and running boundary sensitivity analyses.

hr.q: How do you respond when assigned a task with vague requirements or incomplete information?
hr.how: Demonstrate proactive ownership: outline reasonable technical assumptions, document boundary conditions transparently, consult domain subject matter experts, and present structured alternatives to the supervisor.

hr.q: Give an example of a situation where you had to manage competing priorities under tight project deadlines.
hr.how: Use the STAR approach: describe how you evaluated project critical paths, prioritized high-impact engineering deliverables, communicated transparently with teammates, and delivered quality results on schedule.

hr.q: How would you handle a disagreement regarding a process safety calculation with a senior engineer?
hr.how: Emphasize professionalism, intellectual humility, and data-driven debate. Present documented industry standards (API/CGA/EIGA) and rigorous first-principles physics, listening respectfully to their field experience to reach consensus.

hr.q: Where do you see yourself developing professionally at Linde over the next 5 years?
hr.how: Express an ambition to gain deep foundational expertise in plant commissioning and operations, advance to lead process design engineer on world-scale cryogenic ASUs or clean hydrogen projects, and contribute to Linde's operational excellence.

present: Exhibit deep mastery of chemical engineering thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and cryogenic principles.
Display an exceptional, uncompromising focus on process safety, oxygen compatibility, and risk management.
Structure technical responses logically from first principles with dimensional consistency.
Communicate project accomplishments with humility, authenticity, and clear articulation using the STAR format.
Demonstrate passion for industrial decarbonization, hydrogen mobility, and world-class engineering execution.
tips: Revise air separation fundamentals: double column layout, condenser-reboiler heat balance, and argon side-arm columns.
Understand Joule-Thomson expansion, inversion curves, and isentropic expansion in turboexpanders.
Be prepared to discuss oxygen safety principles (CGA G-4.4 / EIGA standards, CFOS cleaning, velocity limits).
Review hydrogen liquefaction principles, ortho-to-para spin isomers, and cryogen storage insulation.
Prepare thoughtful questions about Linde's green hydrogen projects and carbon capture technologies.
